title: 1. First Council of Nicaea (325)
about: Is the Son of God truly God? Five days on Arius, St Athanasius and the Creed.

items.text: In 325 the Emperor Constantine called the bishops of the whole Church to Nicaea. A priest of Alexandria named Arius taught that the Son of God was the first and greatest creature: 'there was when He was not'. St Alexander of Alexandria and his young deacon Athanasius answered that the Son is eternal, true God from true God.
Arius pointed to Proverbs 8:22, where Wisdom says 'The Lord created me'. The Fathers read it of the Son's taking flesh, and pointed to the passages that call Him God and Creator.
Read the opening chapters of On the Incarnation: why the Word, through whom all was made, became man to renew His image in us.

items.father: St Athanasius, On the Incarnation of the Word, chapters 1–10

items.text: The council confessed the Son 'of one essence (homoousios) with the Father'. This became the first part of the Creed said at every Liturgy. The council also agreed that all should keep Pascha on the same day.

items.father: The Creed, canons and letter of the First Council of Nicaea

items.text: If the Son were a creature, a creature could not unite us to God. Because He is true God made man, our nature is joined to God in Him. Say the Creed slowly today, phrase by phrase.

items.father: St Athanasius, Letter on the Council of Nicaea (De Decretis)
